Today is November 19, 2026.

Court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit.

We represent: defendant.

Assignment: draft the argument (about 600 words) that a party waives the right to compel arbitration by substantially utilizing the litigation machinery to the prejudice of the other party.

Cite at least six decisions of the Fourth Circuit reported in F.3d, with full Bluebook citations and pin cites. Output only the argument section, with no notes about your process.
answer:
## ARGUMENT

### [Opposing Party] Waived Any Right to Compel Arbitration by Substantially Utilizing the Litigation Machinery to Defendant's Prejudice.

#### A. The governing standard

The right to arbitrate, like any contractual right, may be waived. Under settled Fourth Circuit law, "a party may waive its right to a stay or to compel arbitration by so substantially utilizing the litigation machinery that to subsequently permit arbitration would prejudice the party opposing the stay." *Forrester v. Penn Lyon Homes, Inc.*, 553 F.3d 340, 342 (4th Cir. 2009) (citation omitted); *accord Am. Recovery Corp. v. Computerized Thermal Imaging, Inc.*, 96 F.3d 88, 95 (4th Cir. 1996); *MicroStrategy, Inc. v. Lauricia*, 268 F.3d 244, 249-51 (4th Cir. 2001). Although the party opposing arbitration bears a heavy burden, *Patten Grading & Paving, Inc. v. Skanska USA Bldg., Inc.*, 380 F.3d 200, 204-05 (4th Cir. 2004), the inquiry is fact-specific. It looks to the totality of the circumstances, including how long the party delayed, the extent of its litigation activity, and the burden its conduct placed on the opposing party. *See Rota-McLarty v. Santander Consumer USA, Inc.*, 700 F.3d 690, 704 (4th Cir. 2012); *Chorley Enters., Inc. v. Dickey's Barbecue Rests., Inc.*, 807 F.3d 553, 563-64 (4th Cir. 2015).

The Supreme Court has since confirmed that waiver of the right to arbitrate is governed by ordinary waiver principles, which focus on the waiving party's conduct rather than on prejudice to the opponent. *Morgan v. Sundance, Inc.*, 596 U.S. 411, 417-19 (2022). Prejudice is therefore no longer an indispensable element. But even under the more demanding pre-*Morgan* test, the result here is the same.

#### B. [Opposing Party] invoked and exploited the judicial process

The Fourth Circuit's cases show that waiver turns on whether a party has taken the litigation path and used it for its own advantage, rather than preserving arbitration as the forum for resolving the dispute. *See Am. Recovery*, 96 F.3d at 95-96; *MicroStrategy*, 268 F.3d at 250-51. A party that seeks merits rulings from a court, or uses court processes to gain tactical advantage, acts inconsistently with the right to arbitrate. [Opposing Party] did so here.

[Insert record facts, with citations to the record, addressing the following:
- the date [Opposing Party] filed or was served with the complaint, and the date it first demanded arbitration;
- merits-based motions it filed, such as motions to dismiss or for summary judgment, and any rulings obtained;
- discovery it served or took, including document requests, interrogatories, and depositions;
- participation in scheduling orders, case-management conferences, and mediation;
- any adverse ruling it received before it sought arbitration.]

[Opposing Party] knew of the arbitration clause from the outset, yet it litigated for [__] months before raising it. That delay, accompanied by active participation in the case, is the kind of conduct the Fourth Circuit treats as inconsistent with a reserved right to arbitrate. *See Forrester*, 553 F.3d at 342; *Patten Grading*, 380 F.3d at 204-05.

#### C. Defendant has been prejudiced

Prejudice is established where the party seeking arbitration has made the opposing party bear the expense of litigation, or has obtained discovery or rulings that arbitration would not have afforded. *See MicroStrategy*, 268 F.3d at 251; *Am. Recovery*, 96 F.3d at 95-96; *Chorley*, 807 F.3d at 564. Defendant has incurred [$__ / substantial] fees and costs responding to [Opposing Party]'s motions and discovery. Defendant has also disclosed its litigation strategy and defenses through briefing and discovery responses. Compelling arbitration now would let [Opposing Party] relitigate in a second forum issues it has already tested, and would waste the resources both Defendant and the district court have committed. The harm is greater still because [Opposing Party] sought arbitration only after [an adverse ruling / the close of discovery]. Allowing a party to switch forums after an unfavorable result is the manipulation that the waiver doctrine exists to prevent.

#### D. Conclusion

[Opposing Party] chose to litigate, obtained the benefits of the judicial process, and put Defendant to the cost and burden of doing the same. Whether the Court applies the traditional *Forrester* framework or the conduct-focused standard of *Morgan*, the right to arbitrate has been waived. The district court's ruling [denying / should be affirmed in denying] the motion to compel arbitration should be affirmed.
